Question: Can agents write, execute, and iterate code in isolated environments? Which runtimes are supported (Python, JS, SQL minimum)?
Response: Yes. GHCP SDK agentic loops can generate and execute code in sandboxed environments. Python is natively supported (GHCP SDK is Python-based). For sandboxed execution: Azure Container Apps or Azure Container Instances provide isolated runtime environments for generated code. The agentic loop generates code (e.g. CV parsing logic, data transformation, analytics queries), executes it in the sandbox, evaluates results, and iterates. SQL execution against data stores (Cosmos DB, Dataverse, Databricks) is supported via MCP tool calls. JavaScript execution is supported in sandboxed Node.js environments. All generated code execution is governed: GHCP SDK hooks log code generation events, Foundry Guardrails can inspect generated code for safety, and the sandbox provides isolation from production systems.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK (code generation), Azure Container Apps/Instances (sandbox), Python/JS/SQL runtimes

Question: Can proven generative code solutions be reviewed, tested, versioned, and promoted into a managed function library with CI/CD; becoming deterministic tools callable by agents?
Response: Yes — this is the core crystallisation mechanism. Pipeline: (1) Agentic loop generates code solution (e.g. CV parsing logic). (2) Solution is captured and submitted for human review via the Control Plane. (3) Reviewed code is committed to Git and registered as a skill in Azure API Center at Design stage. (4) Automated tests run in CI/CD pipeline (unit tests, integration tests, evaluation against test data). (5) Promoted through lifecycle: Design -> Preview -> Production. (6) The crystallised skill is now a deterministic tool callable by future agentic loops — faster, cheaper, and more predictable than LLM-generated logic. (7) If the crystallised skill encounters a novel exception, it falls back to generative orchestration and logs the exception for the next crystallisation cycle. Skills are Git-synced: API Center integrates with GitHub Actions workflows for syncing SKILL.md files from repositories. GHCP SDK hooks ensure agentic loops pick up promoted skills automatically.
Key Technologies: Azure API Center (lifecycle), Git, CI/CD pipeline, GHCP SDK hooks, SKILL.md

Question: Can agents operate headless browsers or VMs to interact with web applications; integrated with enterprise IDAM (Okta/Entra ID)? Can generated automation scripts be reviewed, frozen, containerised?
Response: GHCP SDK supports computer use patterns — the agentic loop can drive a headless browser via Playwright or similar tools to interact with legacy web applications. For enterprise IDAM integration: the headless browser session authenticates via Okta/Entra ID using the Hosted Agent's identity, with Conditional Access policies applying to the browser session. Generated automation scripts follow the crystallisation pipeline: (1) agentic loop generates the script, (2) human reviews via Control Plane, (3) approved script is frozen (immutable), containerised, and registered as a deterministic skill. This is primarily useful for legacy HR systems without APIs. The script governance ensures generated automations are reviewed before production use.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK computer use, Playwright, Entra/Okta IDAM, crystallisation pipeline

Question: Describe the review gate for generated scripts: approval workflow, immutability post-approval, version control, audit trail, execution log retention.
Response: Script governance uses the same skill lifecycle pipeline. (1) Approval workflow: generated scripts are submitted via the Control Plane for human review. API Center lifecycle gate requires approval to promote from Design to Preview to Production. (2) Immutability post-approval: once promoted to Production in API Center, the skill version is immutable. Any modification requires a new version through the full lifecycle. (3) Version control: skills are Git-committed. API Center maintains full version history with author, timestamp, and change description. (4) Audit trail: every script execution is logged in OTEL telemetry — what was executed, by which agentic loop, with what inputs and outputs. GHCP SDK hooks log all tool calls including script executions. (5) Execution log retention: all logs flow to Azure Log Analytics with 7-12 year retention (immutability enforced via Azure Storage export with immutability policies). Script approval decisions are logged with approver identity and timestamp.
Key Technologies: Azure API Center lifecycle, Git version control, OTEL execution logging, Azure Log Analytics
